messages.text: Can you compare five gimbals for the spring wedding season? I need one that holds my mirrorless with the 24-70 and lasts a full day.
On it. I'll check weight, payload, battery life and street price for five current models and write it up as a short report.

Yes - here is the comparison.

**Short version:** Model A and Model C both hold a mirrorless with the 24-70 comfortably. Model E is the lightest but its battery is the first to run out.

| Gimbal | Weight | Payload | Battery | Price |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Model A | 1.1 kg | 3.2 kg | 12 h | $289 |
| Model B | 0.9 kg | 2.5 kg | 10 h | $219 |
| Model C | 1.3 kg | 4.0 kg | 14 h | $349 |
| Model D | 1.0 kg | 3.0 kg | 9 h | $199 |
| Model E | 0.8 kg | 2.0 kg | 8 h | $159 |

The full write-up, with test notes and sample footage links, is here:

{{REPORTS}}\Gimbal comparison, spring 2027.pdf

Next I'm checking which of these are in stock locally.

replyRules.text: Two of the five are in stock locally: Model A and Model D. Model C ships in about a week. I'll add the shop links to the report.
On price alone Model E is the cheapest ($159), but for a full wedding day I'd pick Model A: the battery lasts 12 hours and the payload leaves room for a heavier lens.

replies: Thanks - I've added that to the comparison and will update the report. (This is a demo workspace, so nothing real is being searched.)
